fit_rules.why: No CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md tells agents how this repo works.
Agents that read only AGENTS.md won't see your rules.
Two instruction files; keep one canonical and the other a pointer.
Tests exist, but no CI gate runs them.
No tests detected for agents to verify against.
Some subagents have no tool limits.
A SKILL.md here is over 500 lines.
This repo's settings don't turn on the OS sandbox.

practices.agent_snippet: Keep the skill entrypoint focused; move conditional procedures and references out of the default context when they are not needed for every invocation.
practices.pattern: Keep the skill entrypoint focused and load conditional detail only when the task needs it.
practices.rationale: Lean entrypoints reduce context cost and make the actual operating contract easier to inspect and maintain.
practices.title: Keep skill entrypoints lean

practices.agent_snippet: Describe the capability and its real trigger in the skill description; add an exclusion only when it prevents likely misrouting.
practices.pattern: Describe what a capability does and when it applies without turning its trigger into a catchall.
practices.rationale: Precise triggers reduce accidental activation, missed capabilities, and context spent evaluating unrelated work.
practices.title: Write discriminating skill triggers

practices.agent_snippet: Use skills for reusable reasoning, subagents for isolated specialization, and hooks or CI for behavior that must happen deterministically.
practices.pattern: Put guidance, isolation, and invariant enforcement in the mechanism designed to provide that guarantee.
practices.rationale: Matching mechanism to guarantee prevents advisory text from being mistaken for enforcement or authorization.
practices.title: Choose the control surface

practices.agent_snippet: Give delegated work only the tools, authority, context, and duration required for its result; isolate repository changes when the task warrants it.
practices.pattern: Scope delegated agents by capability, authority, duration, and isolation.
practices.rationale: Least privilege and isolation reduce accidental side effects, but the right boundary depends on the repository and the delegated task's risk.
practices.title: Bound delegated work

practices.agent_snippet: After structural validation, exercise a complex skill on representative tasks and revise it from observed routing or decision failures.
practices.pattern: Validate a reusable capability with realistic use when structural checks cannot show that its decisions are useful.
practices.rationale: Realistic forward use catches routing and decision failures, but a formal behavioral test should match the skill's complexity and consequence.
practices.title: Validate real skill usage

practices.agent_snippet: Route network access from agent-run code through an enforcing proxy and explicit policy — allow, deny, or approve — rather than leaving egress ambient, and confirm a real proxy is in the path before relying on the gate.
practices.pattern: Treat network access from agent-executed work as a capability mediated by an enforcing proxy and policy — allowed, denied, or routed to approval — not an ambient default of running code.
practices.rationale: Gating network egress through an enforcing proxy and explicit policy — allow, deny, or approve — contains exfiltration and supply-chain risk that ambient network access would leave open.
practices.title: Gate network egress from agent-run work

practices.agent_snippet: Before adding a helper, search the repository for an existing capability and explain why it is insufficient if you add a new abstraction.
practices.pattern: Search the repository before introducing a helper or parallel abstraction.
practices.rationale: The search-first heuristic prevents duplicate abstractions, but it must allow a new helper when existing capabilities do not meet the requirement.
practices.title: Search before adding helpers

practices.agent_snippet: Keep the change proportional to the requested behavior; separate required refactoring from unrelated cleanup.
practices.pattern: Keep a change limited to the behavior and evidence needed for the task.
practices.rationale: Narrow scope reduces review and regression risk, but a necessary refactor is appropriate when the requested behavior cannot be correct without it.
practices.title: Make proportional changes

practices.agent_snippet: Produce edits in an explicit, context-anchored format and verify the target context matches before mutating, so a stale or mistargeted change is caught rather than corrupting the file.
practices.pattern: Express an agent-generated edit in an explicit, parseable format with surrounding context.
practices.rationale: An explicit, context-anchored edit format lets the target be checked for a match before mutation, so a stale or mistargeted edit is caught rather than silently corrupting the file.
practices.title: Express edits in an explicit, verifiable format

practices.agent_snippet: Before editing, inspect applicable instructions, repository status, structure, declared commands, and affected paths.
practices.pattern: Inspect repository structure, instruction files, scripts, and declared checks before acting.
practices.rationale: Orientation prevents agents and humans from inventing incompatible conventions or repeating work already represented in the repository.
practices.title: Inspect the repository first

practices.agent_snippet: Keep durable policy canonical and make agent-specific files thin, discoverable adapters rather than disconnected copies.
practices.pattern: Keep durable repository policy canonical and make tool-specific adapters point back to it.
practices.rationale: A discoverable canonical source reduces semantic drift while allowing each tool to receive the syntax and scope it can actually consume.
practices.title: Keep canonical context discoverable

practices.agent_snippet: Test the changed behavior and its plausible failure modes; do not add tests solely to satisfy an arbitrary size threshold.
practices.pattern: Test behavior and risk rather than an arbitrary test-count or line-count target.
practices.rationale: Behavior-focused tests provide stronger evidence than coverage theater while preserving room for judgment on genuinely trivial changes.
practices.title: Test meaningful behavior

practices.agent_snippet: When wiring or registration changes, run the narrowest real-path check that exercises the composition boundary.
practices.pattern: Exercise the real call path or integration boundary when wiring is part of the change.
practices.rationale: End-to-end or integration-level evidence catches registration and composition failures that isolated tests cannot see.
practices.title: Test real wiring

practices.agent_snippet: Run the repository's declared verification gate and report exactly what passed, what was skipped, and what remains unverified.
practices.pattern: Run the repository's real verification gate before claiming a change is complete.
practices.rationale: A real gate makes evidence repeatable, but the consuming repository must define which checks and human acceptance conditions are authoritative.
practices.title: Use the real verification gate

practices.agent_snippet: Make each completion claim match the evidence lane that actually passed, and name any unverified lane.
practices.pattern: Describe completion, validation, and acceptance only as strongly as the evidence supports.
practices.rationale: Evidence-scoped reporting prevents false confidence and preserves the distinction between what was inspected, tested, deployed, and accepted.
practices.title: Match claims to evidence

practices.agent_snippet: Before an escalating or irreversible action, compute an explicit allow/ask/reject verdict from policy, profile, and sandbox availability, and route risky writes to approval rather than running them unchecked.
practices.pattern: Compute whether an action is allowed with an explicit policy, separate from the code that performs it.
practices.rationale: Separating the allow, ask, or reject decision from the action makes authorization auditable and lets risky or non-conforming writes route to approval or refusal instead of running unchecked.
practices.title: Decide permission separately from the action

practices.agent_snippet: Run agent-executed commands inside an OS sandbox with least privilege where a supported backend is enabled, surface violations instead of widening the policy silently, and treat "no sandbox available" as fail-safe rather than permission to run unconfined.
practices.pattern: Run agent-executed commands inside an operating-system sandbox with a least-privilege policy.
practices.rationale: Where a supported OS sandbox backend is enabled, it contains the blast radius of an agent-run command regardless of the agent's intent, and recorded violations make over-broad access visible instead of silent.
practices.title: Confine agent-executed commands in an OS sandbox
